Manager snapshot

These are retrospective league-history stats, not forecasts. All-play win rate asks how often this roster would have beaten every other team each week. Schedule luck is actual win rate minus all-play rate. Lineup capture is started points divided by the best valid lineup available on that week's roster. Draft, addition, and trade callouts use position-adjusted value over replacement (VORP), so a quarterback's larger raw point total does not automatically make him more valuable.

      League charts

      Position scarcity, franchise history, weekly scoring ranges, manager skills, season momentum, and draft-day value. Hover any mark for the underlying data.

      Position scarcity curve

      Season points by positional rank. The labeled dot is the first player beyond that position's drafted pool—the replacement baseline used by VORP.

      A flatter curve means less separation from replacement. That is why raw quarterback points do not automatically imply greater fantasy value.

      Manager performance quadrant

      Underlying weekly strength versus lineup execution. Bubble size is trade volume; gold marks a champion.

      Top-right combines strong rosters with efficient weekly decisions. Click a manager to activate that lens.

      Season journey heatmap

      Every archived week for one manager. Darker cells left more hindsight points on the bench.

      WinLossDarker = more points left

      Click a week to load the exact roster, moves, and start/sit audit in the matchup time capsule.

      Draft value scatter

      Overall pick versus same-position Draft Edge. Higher marks beat the realistic alternatives selected immediately afterward.

      Selecting a manager above highlights that franchise. Click any dot to switch the whole report to its manager.

      Season arc

      See whether a team started slowly, finished strongly, or rode a decisive streak. The line is cumulative win rate; the colored marks are the result of each recorded matchup.

      —Season shape
      —First four
      —Last four
      —Longest win streak
      —Longest skid
      WinLossTie or other

      “Slow start” means the team improved by at least 20 percentage points after its first four games; “fast start, faded” is the reverse. Click any week to open its matchup time capsule.

      Team trajectory

      One franchise at a time: regular-season scoring rank versus final finish. Rank No. 1 is at the top.

      Final finishRegular-season scoring rank

      A final-finish line above the scoring line means the team finished better than its points rank; below it means the opposite.

      Weekly scoring range

      Compare each franchise's weekly floor, typical score, and ceiling. Boxes cover the middle 50% of recorded starter scores; whiskers run from the 10th to 90th percentile.

      A narrow box means consistency; a long right whisker signals spike-week upside. Click a manager row to activate that lens.

      Draft DNA

      Average same-position Draft Edge by position and draft phase for one manager.

      Positive edgeNegative edge

      Early = rounds 1–3, middle = 4–7, late = 8+. Each cell shows average Draft Edge; hover for pick count.

      Team-building leaderboard

      Separate league ranks for drafting, trading, and waiver value—there is no arbitrary overall grade.

      Raw values are normalized per season. Draft = total core-position Draft Edge. Trade = cumulative net ROS VORP from the ledger. Waivers = VORP from each manager's eight best qualifying additions. Hover each rank for the raw value and sample.

      ROS VORP is closest to a conventional trade-analyzer outcome. Held and Started columns handle flips, injuries, and unused bench assets. Roster reconstruction requires reciprocal movement between the same teams/week after removing adds and waivers.

      Safe-to-share data policy

      • No ESPN cookies, emails, SWIDs, member IDs, raw API payloads, or internal transaction IDs are embedded.
      • Third-party proprietary rankings are not included. The analysis borrows familiar ideas—optimal-lineup capture, all-play record, and roster-aware trade value—but calculates them only from this league’s ESPN archive.
      • This retrospective VORP approximates FantasyPros’ approach using the first player beyond the number actually drafted at each position as replacement. It uses realized points because historical weekly projections are unavailable.
      • Draft and trade results are hindsight context, not proof that the original decision process was good or bad.
      Generated 2026-07-29 from a local ESPN archive. Tables can be sorted by clicking a column header and downloaded as CSV. This file is self-contained and makes no network requests.
